LESSON: FICTION AND NON - FICTION 7.3.1 FICTION: ANTHOLOGY OF SHORT STORIES FROM KENYA

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.3: Fiction and Non - Fiction 7.3.1 Fiction: Anthology of Short Stories from Kenya
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Fiction and Non - Fiction 7.3.1 Fiction: Anthology of Short Stories from Kenya, part of Strand 7 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 LITERATURE IN ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How do characters in short stories reflect our society? 2. Why should we pick moral lessons from short stories?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Fiction and Non - Fiction 7.3.1 Fiction: Anthology of Short Stories from Kenya together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and problem solving: This is enhanced as the learner uses logical thinking to present the sequence of events

in the short story on a flow chart in class.

● Creativity and imagination: This is nurtured as the learner embraces creative ideas when practising hot seating for various

characters.

Values:
● Social justice: This is enhanced as the learner accords equal opportunities to peers when collaborating to present a summary

of the characters and their relationship with others in a graphic organiser and displays it in the classroom.

● Respect: This is nurtured as the learner appreciates peer’s contributions when picking out the moral lessons from the short

story.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social awareness skills: This is enhanced as the learner collaborates with peers to accomplish group tasks.
